entities.summary: A "world view," or *Weltanschauung* as articulated by German philosophers like Wilhelm Dilthey, represents the fundamental cognitive and evaluative framework through which individuals and societies interpret reality, assign meaning, and guide action. Though formalized in 18th-century German thought, its conceptual roots extend deep into human history, encompassing the integrated systems of thought found in ancient cosmologies, religious doctrines, and philosophical schools across diverse civilizations. This overarching conceptual lens is critical for understanding the collective consciousness and cultural evolution of any historical period, from the Stoic *logos* to the Christian *sacra doctrina*, shaping everything from scientific inquiry to political structures and artistic expression. It acts as the foundational prism through which all human experience, knowledge, and values are filtered, dictating perceptions of time, causality, morality, and the very nature of existence, thereby profoundly influencing societal development and individual identity globally across the Classical Era and beyond.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The concept of a world view is fundamentally world-changing because it underlies all human thought, action, and societal organization, shaping every major historical epoch from ancient empires to modern nation-states. It dictates how civilizations perceive themselves and interact with the world, directly influencing scientific discoveries, religious movements, and political ideologies.
